dedupe_keys.name: data from self reported household impacts of large scale chemical contamination of the public water supply charleston west virginia usa

description: Charles Schade and colleagues publish household survey data on the January 2014 chemical contamination of the public water supply around Charleston, West Virginia. The survey covers 498 households and addresses perceived illness, extra expenses, missed work, risk communication, compliance with water-use advice and access to safe water. Zenodo provides a CSV and a DOCX README, free under CC0, with a link to the describing PLOS ONE paper. These observations can inform household-response assumptions and service-disruption costs in water-emergency simulations. The public summary does not establish detailed sampling weights, variable coding or interview dates; these remain unknown pending documentation review. Reported symptoms and attributed impacts should not be interpreted as confirmed clinical causation. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this event survey. Only metadata were inspected, without downloading household-level responses.
